title: Introduce telemetry-scrub-runner and deferred-metric-compressor for cardinality and privacy control
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: our observability pipeline has grown high-cardinality and leaks customer-identifying fields into downstream metric labels and logs, increasing storage costs and complicating alerting. This PR introduces two cooperating subsystems: 1) telemetry-scrub-runner: a small, pluggable service that applies configurable scrubbing/transformation rules to metric labels and structured logs before they reach long-term storage; 2) deferred-metric-compressor: an aggregator that identifies low-value, high-cardinality metrics and compresses them into compact sketches or time-bucket rollups with an attached fidelity tag so downstream dashboards/alerts can opt into reduced-resolution data. Key features: configurable scrubbing rules (regex + allowlist), annotation tags for provenance, on-the-fly privacy-safe hashing for identifiers, retention-aware compression policies, and a stability-simulator to run replayed traffic and estimate alert impact prior to rollout. Changeset summary: implements the runner service, adds compression adapters for Prometheus/StatsD ingestion, wires a new sidecar for the telemetry ingesters, updates observability dashboards and alerting recipes, and documents the config in the operator charts. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is no-op unless an org enables a rule-set in the Console; compression is opt-in per metric prefix. Rollout plan: staged canary (10% tenants) -> 25% -> 100% over two weeks with automated rollback on fidelity regression. Testing: unit tests for scrub rules and compressor logic, integration tests against a small replaybench with synthetic tenant traffic, and a canary-run in perf-lab. Related work: ENG-2345 (privacy observability), ENG-2398 (cost reduction sprint). Checklist: [x] telemetry-scrub-runner service and API; [x] compressor library with sketch and rollup adapters; [x] Console UI for rule toggles; [x] operator Helm changes and migration notes; [x] integration + load tests; [x] runbook for rollback and fidelity diagnostics. Impact: expected to reduce high-cardinality metric ingestion by ~35% for customers that enable default rules and cut cost for long tail tenants. Monitoring: added an internal fidelity-metric (telemetry.fidelity.score) and a compressor-drop-rate metric to track potential data loss from compression.
